title: SLO regression acceptance and traffic-gating playbook for multi-tenant hosted inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define precise SLOs, automated acceptance checks, and a multi-stage traffic gating playbook to prevent SLO regressions when rolling new runtime/model variants to the hosted inference fleet. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, test plan, and operational runbook items required before a production rollout. Goal: ensure we can ship runtime-1.24 model-serving changes without causing measurable customer-perceived latency or availability regressions across tenant classes.
requirements: Establish deterministic, machine-evaluable SLOs for conversational and embedding endpoints by tenant class (free/standard/enterprise).
Implement pre-flight acceptance checks that run on synthetic and seeded customer workloads and fail fast on SLO breaches before any traffic shift.
Define automated gates for canary progression (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) tied to objective metrics and error-budget burn rates.
Integrate burn-rate-based rollback automation: if burn rate > 4x for 30m or > 2x for 2h, automatically stop progression and revert traffic.
Provide clear manual override steps and escalation path for on-call and SREs.
Document operational dashboards and drilldowns required for release owners and SREs (latency histograms, per-tenant error budgets, request traces).
Scope for this ticket: hosted inference runtime changes and model-variant swaps only. Dedicated/Private environments will adopt the playbook but are out of scope for enforcement changes.
sla_slos: Availability (hosted API, multi-tenant): 99.95% monthly for Standard/Enterprise; 99.5% for Free tier. Availability measured from successful 200/2xx responses across global regions excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
Latency: Conversational endpoints (chat stream first token): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 650ms. Non-streaming generation p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms.
Embeddings batch endpoints: p95 < 1200ms for batch sizes <= 64; single-vector embedding p95 < 120ms.

Error budget: monthly error budget defined as (1 - availability SLO) * total requests per month. For Standard/Enterprise example: 0.05% of requests. Any single sustained burn above 2.5x the remaining budget triggers escalation.

Correctness/quality guard: model-variant switch must not increase top-level application-level regression rate (as defined by a canonical prompt set) by more than 0.5% relative to baseline across sampled customers.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pre-deploy suite passes on staging for 48h of synthetic traffic that mirrors customer distributions (latency/size/sequence-length).
Canary deployment to 1% live traffic shows no SLO violations for 60m and burn rate <= 1.2x baseline for both latency and errors.
Canary to 5% shows stable behavior for 2h and burn rate <= 1.5x baseline; no regressions in canonical prompt set exceeding 0.5%.
Observability artifacts (dashboards) created and linked in the release PR: p50/p95/p99 histograms, per-tenant error-budget trend, request traces aggregated by host and model variant.
Automated rollback triggers are configured and exercised in a dry-run scenario (simulated burst causing expected rollback decision).
Runbook steps for manual rollback, post-mortem template, and customer notification templates are attached to the release.
rollout_gates: Stage 0 (pre-flight/staging): Run synthetic workloads for 48h; gate passes if no SLO breach and no >10% increase in median CPU/GPU utilization on serving hosts.
Stage 1 (canary 1%): Deploy to 2 small regions and mirror 1% production traffic; gate passes if p95 latency <= gate threshold and burn rate < 1.2x for 60m.

Stage 2 (canary 5%): Expand to 5% globally for 2h; gate passes if p95/p99 latency, request error rate, and correctness guard all within thresholds and no single tenant sees >3x baseline error-rate increase.

Stage 3 (ramp 25%): Ramp to 25% for 3h with active monitoring; if burn rate crosses 2x for >30m, halt and revert to previous variant. If no issues, progress to 100% in 2 steps (50% then 100%) with 1h observation windows.

Automated rollback policy: any of the following cause immediate halt and rollback: sustained p99 above threshold for 15m, request error rate increase >0.5% absolute for 30m, or canary-specific burn-rate >4x for 30m.
Manual override: Release owner approval required to ignore an automated gate. Approval must be logged in release notes with justification and mitigation plan.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Release overview with real-time p50/p95/p99, per-tenant error budgets, host resource utilization, and top 10 slowest routes.

Alerts: P99 latency breach alert when >2x SLO for 10m; Pager to on-call SRE if sustained for 15m. Burn-rate alert: when current burn-rate >= 2x projected budget for next 24h, create Sev-1 if >4x for 30m.
Drilldowns: Link from alert to per-tenant and per-model traces, recent deploy metadata, and canary traffic cohorts.
Post-deploy telemetry retention: keep per-candidate metrics at 1s granularity for 48h and 1m granularity for 30d for postmortem analysis.
testing_plan: Load tests: run distributed load harness that exercises mix of short-chat, long-chat, and embeddings with traffic shaping consistent with production percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
Regression tests: canonical prompt set (500 prompts) run against baseline and candidate to measure quality regressions; require <=0.5% regression for acceptance.
Chaos experiments: simulate transient host failures and network latency during canary to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies.
Integration tests: validate end-to-end tracing, error budget accounting, and rollback automation in a staging cluster with mirrored metrics pipeline.
scope_changes: Added explicit correctness/quality guard requirement after initial stakeholder review (2026-01-25) to protect against silent quality regressions that don't show as latency or availability issues.
Narrowed scope to hosted inference only; Dedicated/Private environments will receive guidelines but not enforced rollout automation under this ticket.
Deferred tenant-specific SLA customization UI to a follow-up ticket to avoid scope creep.
tradeoffs: Conservative gates (small canaries, long observation windows) increase release safety but slow time-to-market for urgent fixes. We chose a balanced progression to limit exposure while enabling reasonably fast rollouts.
Strict correctness checks may block model updates that improve latency but slightly change outputs; mitigation is to ship as opt-in model variants first for a subset of customers.
Automated rollback reduces human-in-the-loop errors but may create additional churn for noisy transient signals; thresholds tuned to avoid flapping.
